posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
From Steam, go to your library, then to the list entry for RPGMaker MZ. on the page there is a cog icon, click that, then there's a list item called "Browse Local Files". That should bring up the library folder browser. In there should be a folder called DLC, and inside of that should be all the stuff you're looking for. From there it's just about highlighting the files, right-clicking, selecting "copy" and then going to the appropriate folder in your own project folder, right clicking, and selecting "paste". that folder could be one of many, depending on what it is you got.
Once it's in your files, you should be able to find it in the project by going into either a sound test, the plugins page, or scrolling event images. If you continue to have trouble, please try to be as specific as you can about what's giving you trouble regarding these instructions

No, that has nothing to do with it. I need to remove the tile sets from the file that you don't have, otherwise it will look for graphics that are not there and the game will crash.
It's okay, I'll have that done in a few minutes.
Okay, here is what you do, in this order:
Save your project and close RPG maker, if you have it open.
Go to your project folder*(!!) and open the data folder.
Find "Tilesets.json" and rename it to something else. Anything you like, but "Tilesets-Backup.json" makes it easier to find it back when needed.
Put my "Tilesets.json" in its place.
Open your project.
Now everything should be ready to go.
Note: I strongly recommend doing this in a new project. Just delete all the original art, replace it with your new art.
It's just too bad it doesn't come with battlers. I solved this by editing the front view character in the walking sprite and scale it up to 300%. It's not perfect, but it is the best I could do.
Anyhow, the file is in the zipped folder (because I couldn't upload the json file directly). Enjoy.
IMPORTANT! * Your project folder should be in your documents folder, NOT in your program files. If you are in your program files, and find files like this, than those are NOT the ones you need to replace!!
Just thought I mentioned it. You wouldn't be the first to make that mistake.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Based from the posts so far, the OP has problems understanding some windows operations.
so it might be much easier for him to use the build-in assistants.
Here are the steps to follow:
1) start RMMZ with your project loaded
2) click on the menu "tools - resource manager"
3) select what you want to add on the left side - in the example probably "img/tilesets"
4) click on "DLC.." button in the middle right (do not use the import button)
5) you get a list of your steam DLC as well as some free DLC. please navigate to the folder containing what you want to use
6) select the tilesheet (or whatever else) you want to add and press OK
7) repeat until all tilesheets are added.
now you have the tilesheets - the next step is to make them into tilesets.
1) click on the menu "Tools - Database"
2) click on Tilesets in the left tab-list
3) click on "Change Maximum" at the bottom of the tileset list
4) increase the number of tilesets in your game
5) click on one of the new, unnamed tilesets that now have been added
6) name the tileset and select tilesheets for each slot
ATTENTION: make sure each slot only gets a tilesheet formatted for it. You cannot use a tilesheet formatted for A1 in A4 for example
This should be an easier instruction compared to finding yourself through the window explorer...
